meta.tagline: Your social world belongs in your own hands.
meta.description: Peers-Touch is a decentralized, federated social network and intelligent runtime. Your identity, relationships, and data live in a Station you own; stations interoperate through open protocols, with native apps for desktop and mobile — and no company at the center.

home.eyebrow: Your relationships · Your data · Your station
home.title: Your social world belongs in your own hands.
home.subtitle: Who you know and what you post should belong to you — not sit on a tech giant's servers as data to be mined. On Peers-Touch your identity, relationships, and data live in a Station you own. Stations connect through open protocols into a decentralized federation, where each Station is a personal or community-owned center rather than part of a platform-controlled one.

values.title: Your identity, your call
values.body: Your identity is yours to keep, and you can take it to any station. Move somewhere new and you're still you, with the same people around you.

values.title: Your station, your rules
values.body: You and your community can run your own station and set your own rules. Your data and relationships stay here, not on someone else's servers.

values.title: Connected without walls
values.body: No matter which station each of us is on, we can still follow, message, and see each other — the way different email providers just talk to one another. No single company at the center.

values.title: Native, intelligent, every platform
values.body: Purpose-built desktop and mobile apps are fast, capable, and offline-ready, with an AI runtime and applets on top. Your station syncs everything quietly in the background.

steps.title: You get a station
steps.body: Your identity, relationships, messages, and content live in a station you own — self-host it on a NAS or Raspberry Pi, or join a station you trust.

steps.title: Stations connect
steps.body: Through open protocols, stations follow, message, and federate the way email providers do. People on different stations still reach each other, with no company in the middle.

steps.title: Your devices come alive
steps.body: Native desktop and mobile apps work offline and sync in the background. AI assistants and applets add capability on top, all against data you own.

home.trustTitle: Inspect it, run it, and keep your freedom.

trust.title: Decisions you can inspect
trust.body: Product plans, architecture decisions, acceptance criteria, and source changes are discussed and developed in public on GitHub.

trust.title: Run it where you trust
trust.body: Host a Station on a home NAS, Raspberry Pi, or server you control — or join a hosted Station whose operator you trust.

trust.title: Real desktop and mobile apps
trust.body: Peers is designed for local storage, offline use, background sync, calls, and the capabilities of each device — not as a web wrapper.

trust.title: Stations can actually interoperate
trust.body: Identity, relationships, messages, and federation follow shared open contracts, so one provider cannot trap your community.

product.title: A decentralized network. Your Station is your own center.
product.subtitle: Peers-Touch isn't another app living on someone else's servers. Your Station is the personal center that holds your identity, relationships, and data. Stations interoperate through open protocols, while native apps and an AI runtime bring the network to life on your devices.

network.title: Many Stations, one network — and no landlord.
network.note: Run your own Station, or join one you trust. Either way, you're on the same open network.

points.title: Everyone runs a Station
points.body: It holds your identity, relationships, messages, and media — on a NAS or Raspberry Pi at home, or with a host you trust.

points.title: Stations talk, like email
points.body: Open protocols let Stations follow, message, and reshare across one another as easily as email between different providers.

points.title: Reach anyone, no middleman
points.body: A message leaves your Station and lands on a friend's. Nothing is routed through a company in between.

layers.title: Three parts, all working for you.
layers.note: Use Peers on the devices you already have, move between them without losing your place, and keep your social world on a Station you choose.

items.name: Your apps
items.body: Chat, share, and work with your Agent from desktop or mobile. Peers feels familiar on every device.

items.name: One shared experience
items.body: Your people, conversations, and choices stay consistent as you move between devices.

items.name: Your Station
items.body: Your identity, relationships, messages, and community rules live here. It connects with other Stations without handing control to a platform.

agents.title: An AI that works on your data — not a vendor's cloud.
agents.note: The agent runtime lives on your devices and Station. It reasons over data you own, calls tools, and talks to other agents.

points.title: Grounded in your data
points.body: Conversations, contacts, and files come straight from your Station — private by default, not copied into someone else's cloud.

points.title: Tools and applets
points.body: Take real action and add new skills through portable applets, without touching the core.

points.title: Agents that talk to agents
points.body: Negotiate and collaborate with agents on other Stations over the same open network.

items.title: Direct & group messages
items.body: One-to-one and group chats with reactions and rich media, delivered across Stations and devices.

items.title: Private feed — Moments
items.body: Share with exactly who you choose; posts stay private and end-to-end encrypted.

items.title: AI assistants & agents
items.body: A local-capable assistant with tools and agent-to-agent protocols, grounded in data you own.

items.title: End-to-end encryption
items.body: Keys and encrypted envelopes keep content private, with recovery across your devices and Stations.

items.title: Voice & video calls
items.body: Live one-to-one and group calls, with privacy carried across the federated network.

items.title: Applets
items.body: Portable mini-apps on your Station turn it into a workspace, not just a social space.

roadmap.title: Build the network first. Deepen what it can do next.
roadmap.subtitle: Each phase ships working software you can run and test. Identity and Stations first, then social, privacy, and intelligence.

phases.body: Sign in with GitHub or Google, use the same account on desktop and mobile, connect to any Station.
Add friends across Stations, chat 1-on-1 or in groups with reactions and media, post to a private feed.
outcomes: DM and group chat with reactions

phases.body: End-to-end encrypt every message, make voice and video calls, and keep everything working offline.
Run an AI assistant on your own data, install applets that extend your Station, and open the federation.
outcomes: Personal AI grounded in your data

community.title: Build the network with us.
community.subtitle: Peers-Touch is open source. Join the discussion, run a Station, contribute code or design, or help shape what comes next.

ways.title: Join the discussion
ways.body: Ask a focused question, report a real problem, or challenge a product decision.

ways.title: Run a Station
ways.body: Self-host on a NAS, Raspberry Pi, or server you control and help test federation.

ways.title: Contribute code & design
ways.body: Take a scoped issue across desktop, mobile, Station, docs, or product design.

ways.title: Shape the roadmap
ways.body: Bring a concrete user journey and acceptance result to help decide what ships next.
